collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE I: SONGS, CHANTS, SPEECHES AND WELCOMES (LCA-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola sings, chants and speaks for itself: welcoming a new leader, wishing travelers luck, greeting newcomers and newborns, rallying for hard work, standing up for each other, and arguing about who gets the next verse.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Villagers from different families want to share their own songs at a feast: let each sing alone, or weave them into one.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Over the years, families have come to Isola from many shores, and each has kept a few songs from home. (subject) wants a feast where every family sings one. (friend) thinks it would be even better to weave them all into one great song. (subject) worries some families do not want their songs changed. How should the feast go?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: One after another, the families stand and sing. Some songs are fast, some slow, one is almost entirely clapping. The children try to copy every one and get most of them gloriously wrong. Nobody's song is changed, and everybody's song is heard.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) asks each family for one line. Most say yes. Two families say no, and (friend) respects that. The finished song is strange and lovely, and the families who stayed out sing their own songs afterwards, to loud applause. Nobody is quite sure which part was best.
